_comment: CORS. ADR-0018 (deny by default), ADR-0048 (bounded diagnostics, wildcard
with credentials), ADR-0066 (same-origin clarification, no '*' advice).
ADR-0048 said CORS would be 'gated by cors_contract.json and four thin
runners'. That file never existed. This is it, written from the behaviour
the four frameworks ship after tina4-python #139, with the ADR-0048 clauses
that are still not built listed as OWED rather than quietly dropped.
What a same-origin request is: the request's Origin header, normalised to
scheme://host[:port] with the default port dropped, equals the request's own
origin (its scheme - x-forwarded-proto aware, the same detector the session
cookie trusts - and its Host). Browsers send Origin on every same-origin
POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, so the header's presence alone never makes a
request cross-origin.
Being same-origin only silences the warning. It never adds an
Access-Control-* header and never grants anything a cross-origin caller
would not get: the browser needs no CORS header to read its own origin's
response.
Warnings are keyed by REASON (unconfigured, denied, wildcard_credentials),
never by origin, so a scripted probe sending a thousand invented Origin
headers produces one line per reason and grows no ledger. The first line
still names the origin that triggered it, and suggests adding THAT origin -
never '*', which would open the API to every website to silence one warning.
Every case runs through the framework's real request pipeline with the
framework's real logger captured, no mocks: Python server.handle / TestClient,
PHP Router::dispatch / TestClient, Ruby RackApp#call / TestClient, Node a
real startServer() or TestClient over the real dispatch.
Each proven invariant names a suite per framework and case names that the
four suites carry in their own idiom; scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
normalises and matches them.

invariants.rule: With no TINA4_CORS_ORIGINS configured, a cross-origin request gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. With TINA4_CORS_ORIGINS listing https://allowed.example, a request from https://other.example gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, and a request from https://allowed.example gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://allowed.example.
invariants.why: Deny by default is the ADR-0018 baseline that ADR-0048 and ADR-0066 build on. Proving it in the same suite keeps a later change to the warning path from quietly opening the gate.
cases: a cross origin request is denied by default
only a listed origin is granted

invariants.rule: A request whose Origin equals its own origin (scheme and host, default port dropped) produces no CORS warning and no Access-Control-* header - both with no policy configured and with a policy that lists only some other origin. A request whose Origin differs only by port or scheme is cross-origin.
invariants.why: Issue #139: the unconfigured-CORS warning fired on an app's own single-page front end saving a form, because the check was 'Origin is present' instead of 'Origin is foreign'. The fix must silence the warning without turning same-origin into a grant.
cases: a same origin request is neither warned about nor granted
a different port or scheme is cross origin

invariants.rule: The warning for a refused cross-origin request (unconfigured and denied) names the refused origin, tells the operator how to add THAT origin to TINA4_CORS_ORIGINS, and contains no '*'.
invariants.why: The old unconfigured warning ended with "or '*' to allow any origin". An operator silencing one warning would open the API to every website. The advice has to fit the problem: one origin, added by name.
cases: a refused origin warning names the origin and never advises a wildcard

invariants.rule: Refusing many distinct cross-origin requests for the same reason logs exactly one warning for that reason per process, and no per-origin state is retained: the set of remembered warning keys holds reasons only, never an origin. PHP proves this in one serving process (TINA4_SERVE_FORK=false); see cors-reason-ledger-survives-php-request-forks.
invariants.why: The warn-once ledger was keyed by origin, so every attacker-chosen Origin header added an entry that was never freed and another log line. ADR-0048 requires bounded diagnostics with no per-origin ledger.
cases: many refused origins produce one warning per reason and no per origin ledger

invariants.rule: A default PHP app applies the CORS policy without the app calling Router::use(CorsMiddleware::class), as Python, Ruby and Node do. OWED: PHP still needs the explicit registration; the PHP runner registers it the documented way.

Under Tina4's PHP socket server, which forks a child per request by default, one reason still logs one warning per serving process. OWED: each forked child starts with an empty ledger, so every refused request logs its line (the ledger never grows; it dies with the child). The one-warning-per-reason property is proven with TINA4_SERVE_FORK=false, the model a pool worker or PHP-FPM worker follows.

TINA4_CORS_ORIGINS='*' together with TINA4_CORS_CREDENTIALS=true fails application startup with an error naming both settings. OWED: all four still warn once for this reason and send the response without the credentials header.
An allowed cross-origin response carries Access-Control-Expose-Headers, default X-Request-ID, configurable. OWED: no framework emits it yet.
One immutable CORS policy is resolved after .env is loaded and its six typed TINA4_CORS_* keys are validated at startup; an invalid value fails startup. OWED: not proven in any framework.
